comment: MiniDAQ's problem reports (Chapter 14). tools/anomalies.py checks every report and generates known-anomalies.md from the open ones. Dates are when the book found the problem.

reports.title: A number outside the range of double crashed the configuration reader
reports.found: 2026-10-24, Chapter 7, fuzz_config
reports.description: json::out_of_range (406) escaped the reader, which caught only json::parse_error; '6e688' ended the process.

evaluation.rationale: A crash during configure is a lost scan if it happens at the scanner; no wrong value was ever accepted.

resolution.change: The reader catches json::exception.
resolution.verification: Config.NumberOverflowIsAnErrorNotACrash; fuzz_config

reports.title: A sequence jump of 2^31 was counted as two billion lost packets
reports.found: 2026-10-24, Chapter 9, fuzz_packet
reports.description: Serial-number arithmetic is undefined for a distance of exactly 2^31; the tracker took the jump as a gap.

evaluation.rationale: Loss counters are how an operator judges a scan's completeness; a false count of two billion lost packets hides the real loss.

resolution.change: A jump beyond the maximum gap is a restart of the numbering (a resynchronization), not a loss.
resolution.verification: SequenceTracker test for SRS-RDO-006; fuzz_packet

reports.title: A new run could not open its UDP port while the previous run's detector held it
reports.found: 2026-10-24, Chapter 9 measurements
reports.description: The service created the new run's ports before it released the previous run's, so a second run failed with 'address in use'.

evaluation.rationale: The second scan of a session could not start: a delay, and a repeated injection if the tracer decays meanwhile.

resolution.change: The service releases the previous run's pipeline and ports before it creates new ones.
resolution.verification: UdpDetector test for SRS-RDO-012

reports.title: take_all_goods counted a pair twice with per-single windows
reports.found: 2026-10-24, Chapter 10 development
reports.description: With a window per single, the pair (a, b) was formed from a's window and again from b's.

evaluation.rationale: Duplicated prompts bias the counts and the image quantitatively without any visible sign.

resolution.change: Only (opener, later single) pairs are resolved in each window.
resolution.verification: CoincidenceSorter tests for SRS-SRT-002, SRS-SRT-003 and SRS-SRT-009

reports.title: SOUP: nlohmann/json 3.11.3 parses an integer as a float if the C library sets errno during a successful conversion
reports.found: 2026-10-25, Chapter 14 SOUP review
reports.description: Fixed upstream in 3.12.0 (#4506): 3.11.3 treats any nonzero errno after strtoull or strtoll as a failed integer conversion, 3.12.0 only ERANGE. The Chapter 14 review assumed that an errno left by poll() could trigger it; reading the lexer in Chapter 16 showed that errno is reset immediately before the conversion, so only a C library that sets errno on success can trigger it, which POSIX forbids.

evaluation.rationale: The configuration reader requires integers, so such a value would be rejected with a config_error and no wrong setting accepted; with a POSIX C library the defect cannot occur.

resolution.change: CR-0002: nlohmann/json 3.12.0.
resolution.verification: All CI presets, fuzz_config and fuzz_protocol smoke runs, docs.soup

reports.title: A port fault is noticed up to 20 ms late
reports.found: 2026-10-24, Chapter 6 design
reports.description: The service's monitor polls the ports every 20 ms, so a run continues for up to 20 ms after a detector or sink fault.

evaluation.rationale: Data acquired in those 20 ms after a fault is part of a run that ends in a fault anyway; the fault is reported and the run is not used. No data is presented as complete.

reports.decision: Release with it. Reviewed against the risk file for release 0.3.0: a faulted run is incomplete in its integrity verdict whatever the delay (assess_integrity, RC-01), and H-05 covers the interrupted scan; 20 ms more data in a run that ends in a fault changes neither sequence of events nor harm, so no hazard needs a faster reaction. Chapter 15 was to decide this and did not; the release review did.

reports.title: The sorter holds its last 104 ns of singles until more data arrives
reports.found: 2026-10-24, Chapter 10 design
reports.description: A single can only be judged when a later single shows that its window is closed. A source that falls silent leaves up to the window plus the delay of singles in the sorter until the end of the run.

evaluation.rationale: The singles are processed at the end of the run, so no coincidence is lost; only their latency grows while the source is silent.

reports.decision: Release with it; time markers from the readout would flush the sorter (Chapter 23).

reports.title: The control API has no authentication or encryption
reports.found: 2026-10-24, Chapter 6 design
reports.description: Any local process that can connect to 127.0.0.1:7700 can configure, start and stop acquisitions.

evaluation.rationale: A local attacker or a misdirected script can stop a scan or change its settings; the audit trail records it but does not prevent it.

reports.decision: Do not release for use beyond a test bench before Chapter 17's controls are in place.

resolution.change: Token authentication with observer and operator roles, TLS 1.3, secure defaults and API 2.0 (CR-0004, ADR 0014); hazard H-08 closed.
resolution.verification: ControlServer.AnIntruderCannotStopARunningScan, ControlServer.TheTokenNeverCrossesTheNetworkInClear and the other tests of SRS-SEC-001 to SRS-SEC-009

reports.title: Simulation code is linked into the shipped server
reports.found: 2026-10-25, Chapter 14 software item classification
reports.description: The synthetic source and the detector simulator are part of minidaq_core, so minidaq_server contains them and a configuration can select them.

evaluation.rationale: A clinical acquisition configured with a simulated source would produce plausible but invented data. The run record states the source type and metadata carries 'simulated', so the data is identifiable.

reports.decision: Release with it for 0.3.0 (MiniDAQ is a teaching project); a product build excludes the simulator or refuses it outside service mode.

reports.title: Pipeline.DropPolicyCountsEveryLostWord failed on a fast CI runner
reports.found: 2026-10-24, Chapter 7, GitHub CI
reports.description: The test assumed that a debug build's sink is slower than its source, so that the drop policy drops; on a fast runner the sink kept up, nothing dropped, and the test failed.

evaluation.rationale: A defect of the test, not of the pipeline: the drop policy was correct. A test that fails at random teaches people to rerun it, which can hide a real failure; that is the reason for CAPA-0001.

resolution.change: 7f01a94: the sink waits until the source has read everything, so the test no longer depends on relative speeds. Recorded as a problem report in Chapter 16 (internal audit, finding A-4).
resolution.verification: Pipeline.DropPolicyCountsEveryLostWord; the stress run in measurements/ch16/

reports.title: FastSorter.FastEnough failed during a CI run on the shared book machine
reports.found: 2026-10-25, Chapter 12, ci/run_all.sh
reports.description: Exercise 10.4's acceptance test compared the run times of two sorters measured one after the other; a slow spell of the shared virtual machine during one of them changed the ratio.

evaluation.rationale: An exercise test of speed, not a test of MiniDAQ; no requirement was affected. Same cause as MDQ-PR-010.

resolution.change: 3ea28f5: the two sorters run interleaved, best of seven, so a slow spell affects both. Recorded as a problem report in Chapter 16 (internal audit, finding A-4).
resolution.verification: FastSorter.FastEnough in exercises/ch10/e4_fast_sorter

reports.title: The status gained fields without a new minor version of the control API
reports.found: 2026-10-25, Chapter 16 internal audit (finding A-3)
reports.description: detector_counters (Chapter 9), sorter (Chapter 10), sink_counters (Chapter 12) and integrity (Chapter 15) were added to the status while every response still said "api": "1.0", against the rule of ADR 0003 that new fields come with a minor version.

evaluation.rationale: The integrity verdict is a risk control (RC-01, RC-05): a client cannot tell whether a status without it comes from an older server or is incomplete. No client misread a status, because the only clients are MiniDAQ's own.

resolution.change: CR-0003: control API 1.1 with the status fields listed in status_fields (ADR 0013).
resolution.verification: ControlProtocol.StatusFieldsMatchTheApiVersion (SRS-CTL-033)

reports.title: An auth request whose token is not a string ended the control server
reports.found: 2026-10-25, GitHub CI fuzz-smoke (fuzz_protocol) on commit 393693d, after Chapter 17
reports.description: authenticate() read the token with req.value("token", std::string{}), which throws json::type_error when the key is present with another type. Nothing caught it, so one line such as {"cmd":"auth","token":5} from a client that had not authenticated ended minidaq_server (reproduced: abort, exit status 134).

evaluation.rationale: It interrupts a running scan (H-05) without a token, so for availability it bypasses the control of H-08: a process on the PC, or on the network when the server is bound beyond loopback, could end an acquisition. The files written so far stay readable (H-03). Found before release 0.3.0; no released version has it.

resolution.change: The token is read only when it is a string; any other value is an unknown token. The input is in the fuzz seed corpus. CAPA-0003 for the cause.
resolution.verification: ControlProtocol.EveryFieldOfEveryTypeIsAnswered (SRS-CTL-034), ControlProtocol.AuthenticationInTheProtocolLayer, ControlServer.AnUnknownTokenClosesTheConnection

reports.title: The pipeline's throughput evidence was stale and its regression gate never ran
reports.found: 2026-10-25, release checks for 0.3.0 on commit 5fa917b (tools/perf_gate.py run by hand)
reports.description: The performance budget and the verification of SRS-PERF-020 quoted 86 M words/s for the whole pipeline, measured at tag ch05. Since commit b4422de (Chapter 10) the pair stage is the coincidence sorter and the pipeline runs at about 39 M words/s on the reference machine (BM_Pipeline 0.44 of the baseline). The gate that should have reported it, .github/workflows/perf.yml, runs only on a self-hosted runner labelled perf, which does not exist, so it never ran and nothing reported that.

evaluation.rationale: SRS-PERF-020 is still met: 37.9 M words/s is 3.8 times the 10 M singles/s it asks for. A pipeline slower than its input loses singles, and losses are counted and reported (RC-01, H-01), so a slower pipeline cannot lose data silently. The defect is in the evidence, not in the software.

resolution.change: Performance budget version 2 and SRS version 6 with the measurement of release 0.3.0; the BM_Pipeline entries of benchmarks/baseline/book-vm.json replaced; tools/release_checks.sh runs the gate before each release (SDP version 4). CAPA-0004 for the cause.
resolution.verification: measurements/release-0.3.0/perf-pipeline.txt, perf-current.json, perf-gate.txt and pipeline-attribution.txt

reports.title: The class B items ctl and server have no automated test
reports.found: 2026-10-25, Chapter 18 coverage report per software item (tools/coverage.py)
reports.description: The unit tests run neither program. The server's main() (item server: options, security settings, start-up token, shutdown on a signal) has no profile at all, and an early version of tools/coverage.py left it out of the table. The unit tests reach 6 of the 237 lines of minidaq_ctl and none of its 126 branches: no test starts the client. Its parts are tested where they live (TlsContext, TlsStream, read_secret and the control protocol), but not how the client puts them together: that it verifies the server certificate before it sends the token when --tls-ca is given, refuses an unreadable token file, and reports a server that closes the connection.

evaluation.rationale: The client's certificate check is part of the control of HZ-4 (Chapter 17, CR-0004): a client that sent its token before the check would hand an operator token to an impostor. The check itself is tested (TlsStream.ClientVerifiesTheServer), and the client code that calls it was changed and reviewed under CR-0004, so the gap is in the evidence for the composition, not a known defect.

resolution.change: System tests run minidaq_ctl against minidaq_server in their own processes (Chapter 19): exit status, roles, wait, TLS with the right CA and two impostor servers that must receive no byte, shutdown on a signal, refused options and the configuration given at start-up (SRS-CTL-040 to SRS-CTL-044).
resolution.verification: system.control in all six presets. Coverage with the system tests (measurements/ch19/coverage): ctl 81.9% of lines and 77.0% of branches (from 2.5% and 0%), server 80.4% and 81.1% (from not run); the branches not taken are reviewed in measurements/ch19/README.md.

reports.title: The 0.3.0 release commit failed CI: the release record was in no clause of the design file
reports.found: 2026-10-25, Chapter 18 local test run (docs.design_file), then GitHub CI runs 40216164998 and 40216375761
reports.description: The release checks ran on 57ef123, a clean commit before the release commit. The release commit e32e702 added docs/regulatory/releases/0.3.0.md, the first file in that directory, and no clause of docs/regulatory/qms/design-file.json listed it, so docs.design_file failed in every preset and the document-control job failed on e32e702 and 37af8f4. The release was packaged and tagged locally without waiting for CI on the release commit.

evaluation.rationale: No code changed between 57ef123 and 37af8f4: the release commit adds documents and evidence, and the second commit changes a table in the book. Every software test passed on 57ef123 and on GitHub; the failing tests check the index of documents, not the software.

resolution.change: Commit 0262322 lists docs/regulatory/releases/ as evidence for clause 7.3.8. SDP version 5, section 8: a release is tagged and packaged only after CI on the release commit itself is green.
resolution.verification: tools/design_file.py . --check passes on 0262322; GitHub CI on 0262322.

reports.title: Two runs with the same seed wrote different records: singles with equal times split across batches
reports.found: 2026-10-25, Chapter 19 system test GoldenExact (two acquisitions with seed 1 through minidaq_server)
reports.description: The sort stage orders each batch by time and then crystal (Chapter 3), so a sorted batch is a function of the batch. Two singles with the same time that fall into two batches keep the order in which they arrived, and the batches are cut by time (max_batch_delay_us), so where they fall changes from run to run. The coincidence sorter then took the earlier-arriving single as the first of the pair, so crystal_a and crystal_b (and the energies) of a pair with dt 0 could be swapped: in the first two runs compared, the records were equal up to number 135,698 of 231,650, a pair with dt 0. Counts, rates and spectra were unchanged. Each unit met its own specification; no unit test or property could see the defect, because it is in how the two units are put together.

evaluation.rationale: Both orders describe the same coincidence: the line of response, the energies and the time are the same, and a time difference of 0 has no sign. An image does not change. What breaks is reproducibility: a regression test against golden data cannot tell this from a real change, and a field problem cannot be replayed exactly.

resolution.change: The coincidence sorter puts singles with equal times in crystal order as they arrive (CoincidenceSorter::insert), so its output is a function of the singles whatever the batches; SRS-SRT-013 (SRS version 8). The reference model of the properties orders ties the same way, the sorter generator makes ties common, and the property TheOrderOfTiesDoesNotMatter permutes them.
resolution.verification: Properties.TheOrderOfTiesDoesNotMatter and TheSorterFindsWhatTheReferenceFinds fail without the change and pass with it; the system tests GoldenExact (same seed, and small batches with short delays) pass in every preset.

reports.title: The readout system test counted a packet both delayed and duplicated as a late packet
reports.found: 2026-10-25, Chapter 19, recordings for Exercise 19.1 with 5% of each kind of link damage (minidaq_send seed 8)
reports.description: LinkFaults (used by minidaq_send) can delay and duplicate the same packet: it sends the copy on time and the original late. The late original is then a duplicate (stale), not a packet that came after its gap was given up. The system test test_every_damaged_packet_is_accounted_for took every delayed packet that was not reordered as too late, so with 5% of each damage packets_lost and packets_stale were 2 lower than it expected (in one run of seed 8, 108 and 105 against 110 and 107: the run had 2 such packets). The test passed only because its own run (1% of each, seed 5) had no such packet, and minidaq_send did not report the overlap, so no test could account for it. The server's counters were right.

evaluation.rationale: A defect in a test tool and a test, not in the shipped software: the server's link counters were correct. Its risk was a system test that would have failed on a correct server, or passed on a wrong one, at higher damage rates.

resolution.change: LinkFaultCounts counts delayed_duplicated, minidaq_send reports it ('both delayed and duplicated N'), and the readout system test subtracts it from the late packets. A second system test runs with 5% of each kind of damage and requires at least one such packet.
resolution.verification: system.readout: test_every_damaged_packet_is_accounted_for and test_a_packet_both_delayed_and_duplicated_is_a_duplicate pass in every preset; Exercise 19.1's recordings balance with the corrected identity.

reports.title: Under load, the sequence tracker counted a late copy of a held packet as reordered
reports.found: 2026-10-25, Chapter 19 system test test_a_packet_both_delayed_and_duplicated_is_a_duplicate, which failed in 1 run of the coverage report and in 8 of 8 runs with the CPUs loaded
reports.description: SequenceTracker::offer counted a packet as reordered whenever it arrived after a higher sequence number, before it checked whether the packet was a copy of one already held. A packet that the link both delayed and duplicated, whose on-time copy was still held behind an earlier gap, was then counted in packets_reordered and in packets_stale. packets_reordered is documented as 'arrived after a higher sequence number, and was still used'. With the server reading in larger batches under load, packets are held longer and the case becomes common: in the failing runs packets_reordered was one or two too high, and the accounting identity of the readout system test failed by the same amount. Delivery, the loss count and the stale count were right.

evaluation.rationale: packets_reordered is a diagnostic counter: it does not enter the integrity verdict, and no data was lost, duplicated or delivered out of order. A wrong diagnostic misleads the investigation of a link problem, so it is fixed.

resolution.change: The tracker counts a packet as reordered only when it is delivered or held, not when it is dropped as stale.
resolution.verification: SequenceTracker.ALateCopyOfAHeldPacketIsNotReordered fails without the change and passes with it; system.readout passed 8 of 8 runs with the CPUs loaded (it failed 8 of 8 before).

whys: packets_reordered was one or two too high under load: a late copy of a held packet was counted as reordered.
offer() decided 'reordered' from the sequence number alone, before it checked whether the packet was already held.
The counter's definition ('arrived after a higher sequence number, and was still used') was written in the documentation, but the code tested only the first half of it.
No unit test combined delay with duplication while a packet was held; the case needs a gap and a copy at once, which the example tests did not construct and short runs rarely produced.
root_cause.cause: A counter implemented from half of its definition, with no test of the combination of faults that tells the halves apart.
root_cause.escape: The unit tests injected one fault at a time; the system test with a loaded machine was the first to hold packets long enough for both faults to meet.

reports.title: The readout system tests depended on a receive buffer the CI runners do not have
reports.found: 2026-10-25, GitHub Actions runs of 68a63e2 and 8d115d8: system.readout failed in the presets debug and tsan and passed in the other four and on the reference machine
reports.description: Two readout system tests send their stream as fast as possible (minidaq_send --speed 0). On the reference machine net.core.rmem_max is 4 MiB, the server is granted a 4 MiB receive buffer and the burst fits. GitHub's ubuntu-24.04 runners keep Ubuntu's default of 212,992 B: the kernel dropped datagrams of the burst before the slower debug and tsan builds read them, the server counted them as lost, and the tests waited 30 s for datagrams that never came. The tests measured the machine. CI ran ctest without --output-on-failure, so its log named the failing test but not the reason; the failure was reproduced by setting rmem_max to the default on the reference machine. The receive buffer is part of the installation (ADR 0009), but the system test plan did not state it as part of the test environment.

evaluation.rationale: A defect of the test environment and its specification, not of MiniDAQ: the server granted what the kernel allowed, reported the small buffer in its detector description, and counted every dropped datagram as lost, as SRS-RDO requires.

resolution.change: The readout tests check the granted receive buffer before they send and fail at once, naming net.core.rmem_max, if it is below 4 MiB; CI sets rmem_max to 4 MiB as the acquisition PC is installed and runs ctest with --output-on-failure; the system test plan states the setting in its environment.
resolution.verification: With rmem_max at 212,992 B the tests fail immediately with that message (4 of 4 runs); with 4 MiB they pass; the GitHub Actions run of the correcting commit passes in all six presets.

whys: system.readout failed in two presets on GitHub and passed on the reference machine.
The kernel dropped datagrams of a full-speed burst before the slower builds read them.
The runners' net.core.rmem_max is 212,992 B, the reference machine's 4 MiB, and the test assumed the latter.
The system test plan described the programs under test but not the host settings they depend on, although ADR 0009 makes the receive buffer part of the installation.
root_cause.cause: A test environment that was not specified: a setting of the installation, required by the design, was left out of the test plan.
root_cause.escape: Every machine the tests had run on so far had the large buffer; CI logs without --output-on-failure hid the reason for a day.

reports.title: Two jobs of the new CI checks failed on their first run: a script not executable, a listing that did not parse
reports.found: 2026-10-25, GitHub Actions run of 447cc4a (Chapter 20): the jobs perf-ab and reproducible-build failed; the reproducibility check had also failed on the reference machine
reports.description: tools/perf_ab.sh was committed without its executable bit, so the perf workflow stopped with 'Permission denied' before it compared anything. tools/repro_check.sh compared the two packages correctly and printed 'identical', then listed the programs with a Python one-liner whose escaped quotes, inside single quotes, reached Python literally; it did not parse, and the script, run with set -e, failed. Neither defect was on a path that a test exercised: the tests of the release package call tools/release_bundle.py directly, and no test ran the two shell scripts.

evaluation.rationale: Defects of verification tools that made them fail, never pass: no result was reported as better than it was, and no release depended on them.

resolution.change: perf_ab.sh is executable; tools/check_tools.py fails for a shell script in tools/ or ci/ without its executable bit (CTest docs.tools and the static-analysis job); the program listing is a subcommand of tools/release_bundle.py ('programs') with a test, and repro_check.sh calls it.
resolution.verification: check_tools.py reports perf_ab.sh with the bit removed and passes with it set; test tools.release_bundle covers the listing; tools/repro_check.sh passes on the reference machine; the GitHub Actions run of the correcting commit runs both jobs to their result.

whys: Two new CI jobs failed on their first run.
perf_ab.sh lacked its executable bit, and a Python one-liner in repro_check.sh did not parse.
Both scripts had been run by hand through an interpreter (bash script.sh) or edited after the last run, never as CI runs them.
No test ran the shell scripts; the tests covered the Python they call, not the scripts themselves.
root_cause.cause: Release tooling in shell scripts that had no tests of their own and were first run as CI runs them in CI.
root_cause.escape: The review checked the scripts' logic, not their mode bits or quoting, which only running them shows.

reports.title: Exercise 5.2's speed test had a budget in nanoseconds that held only on the reference machine
reports.found: 2026-10-25, GitHub Actions run of b9234db: ch05/e2_hotspot/solution/EventSource.FastEnough failed in the preset gcc-cxx23 at 18.16 ns per single against 18 ns; the run of the next commit passed
reports.description: The acceptance test of Exercise 5.2 required at most 18 ns per single, a third of the starter's 53.5 ns on the book's machine. The solution takes about 13 ns there with GCC 13, but a GitHub runner is another machine with another CPU, and its time came within 1% of the budget, so the test passed or failed by chance. The budget stood for 'three times faster than the starter', measured on one machine and then applied to all.

evaluation.rationale: An exercise test, not a test of MiniDAQ; it could fail a correct solution but not pass a slow one on the reference machine.

resolution.change: The test times a copy of the starter's algorithm in the same process, interleaved with the solution, best of 7 runs each, and requires a third of its time; EX_NS_PER_SINGLE still sets a fixed budget. The exercise, its README, Chapter 5 and the solution notes say so; Chapter 20 uses it as an example of a flaky test.
resolution.verification: On the reference machine the solution takes 12.7 to 13.2 ns against 47 to 50 ns for the reference with GCC (ratio 3.7 or more), and 16.6 to 17.0 ns against 258 to 261 ns with Clang; the starter fails (45 ns against 45 ns).

whys: Exercise 5.2's speed test failed on a GitHub runner at 18.16 ns against 18 ns.
Its budget was an absolute time measured on the book's machine.
The intent, 'three times faster than the starter', was written down as a number that holds on one CPU only.
Performance acceptance criteria had no rule saying whether they are absolute (a requirement) or relative (a comparison).
root_cause.cause: A relative criterion written as an absolute number.
root_cause.escape: On the reference machine the solution had a margin of 30%; a runner with another CPU removed it.

reports.title: The performance gate passed over benchmarks that did not run, so its coverage depended on the CI runner's CPU
reports.found: 2026-10-26, GitHub Actions perf runs of 23c40ab and 7654434: the gate listed five of the six gated benchmarks on an AMD EPYC 7763 and six on an AMD EPYC 9V74
reports.description: BM_EnergyFilter/3/50/0/4096 measures the AVX-512 energy filter kernel and reports an error ('kernel not available on this CPU') on a CPU without AVX-512. tools/perf_gate.py ignores benchmark entries with an error, by design for the reference machine, where every gated benchmark runs, and printed nothing about them. GitHub's ubuntu-24.04 runners come with different CPU models, so a push could be compared on all six benchmarks or on five, without a message. Commit 7654434 first described the cause wrongly, as a benchmark missing from the base side only; tools/perf_ab.sh's count of the runs of each side showed both sides with the errored entries.

evaluation.rationale: A gap in the coverage of a verification tool: a regression of one kernel could go unreported on some runners. The release checks run the gate on the reference machine, where the kernel runs.

resolution.change: perf_gate.py lists every benchmark that reported an error, with its message, after the verdicts; perf_ab.sh lists the runs of each side and stops if the sides differ. Chapter 20 describes the case.
resolution.verification: A run with an errored benchmark is listed as 'not run: kernel not available on this CPU' (checked by hand with a constructed result; tools.perf_gate passes); the next perf run on GitHub shows the line on a runner without AVX-512.

whys: The perf gate judged five benchmarks on some runners and six on others, without a message.
The AVX-512 kernel reports an error where the CPU lacks AVX-512, and the gate skipped errored entries silently.
Skipping was designed for the reference machine, where every gated benchmark runs, and nobody listed what was skipped.
The gate reported what it judged and nothing about what it did not judge.
root_cause.cause: A verification tool whose coverage was implicit: it did not report the checks it skipped.
root_cause.escape: The first diagnosis, in commit 7654434, guessed a cause from one side of the comparison; counting both sides' runs showed the real one.

reports.title: Every build of Part IV said it was version 0.3.0, the release, because VERSION was never moved to 0.4.0-dev
reports.found: 2026-10-26, Chapter 21: the first crash report of minidaq_server built from main said 'version: 0.3.0'
reports.description: VERSION holds the version that every program reports (hello, the crash report, the list-mode files' software field). After releases 0.1.0 and 0.2.0 the first chapter of the next Part set it to the next -dev version. After release 0.3.0 no commit did: Chapters 16 to 20 were built as 0.3.0, so a list-mode file written by any build of main named the released version, and a crash report of an unreleased build would have sent an investigator to the release's code. The build ID tells the builds apart, but nothing compared the version with the commit. The same stale version kept the SOUP check quiet: it asks for a known-anomaly review dated for the current minor version, and the current minor version still read 0.3.

evaluation.rationale: No release was affected: 0.3.0 was built from its release commit. The defect misidentifies development builds, which matters for the traceability of data and of field reports (development plan section 5), not for the data itself.

resolution.change: VERSION is 0.4.0-dev. tools/check_version.py (CTest docs.version) fails when VERSION is a release version outside its release commit, or a -dev version not later than the newest release record; the release procedure of Chapter 20 relies on it. The SOUP known-anomaly reviews for 0.4 that the corrected version asked for are recorded (SOUP list, version 6).
resolution.verification: tools.check_version covers the rules, including this case (Version.test_a_release_version_after_its_release_commit_fails); check_version.py fails on the commit before the change and passes after it.

whys: The crash report of a build of main said 0.3.0.
VERSION still said 0.3.0, five chapters after the release.
Moving to the next -dev version was a habit of the first chapter of each Part, not a step of the release procedure.
Nothing checked that the version a build reports matches the commit it was built from.
root_cause.cause: A manual step that no procedure named and no check enforced.
root_cause.escape: The version appears in outputs that nobody read for it until a crash report put it next to the build ID.

reports.title: Chapter 20's seven code listings used a syntax the book's filter does not know, and the book build did not fail
reports.found: 2026-10-26, Chapter 21: the first EPUB build with Chapter 21 showed that its listings, written like Chapter 20's, were not expanded
reports.description: The book pulls every listing from the repository with book/filters/include-code.lua, which expands a fenced block with an include attribute. Chapter 20 wrote its seven listings as a plain fenced block holding a line '!include PATH snippet=NAME', a syntax nothing implements. Pandoc printed that line as the listing, so the published text of Chapter 20 at tag ch20 showed seven one-line placeholders instead of the code it discusses. The strict build (NEUROLF_STRICT=1) fails on a missing file or snippet, but a block without the attribute was not a listing to the filter, so nothing failed; the EPUB check (epubcheck) validates structure, not content.

evaluation.rationale: A defect of the book's build, not of MiniDAQ. No release was affected: Chapter 20 is not yet in a released edition (0.4.0 will be the first).

resolution.change: The fourteen listings of Chapters 20 and 21 use the include attribute. The filter now counts a fenced block that starts with '!include' as a missing listing, so the strict build fails on it.
resolution.verification: With the corrected filter, pandoc in strict mode fails with 'not an include attribute' on a block in the old syntax (exit 83); with the old filter the same input passed (exit 0). book/build.sh builds both books with no missing listing.

whys: Chapter 20's listings were printed as one-line placeholders.
They were written in a syntax that the filter does not implement.
The filter recognized only its own syntax and passed every other block through silently, so a mistyped listing was not an error.
No check compared the listings the text intends with the listings the build expanded.
root_cause.cause: A build step that accepts input it does not understand without saying so.
root_cause.escape: Nothing that runs on every change builds the book: the code's CI does not, and Chapter 20 was tagged on the code's CI alone. The book build that would have shown the placeholders runs at a Part's release.

reports.title: Exercise 21.5's solution found no result with the git of the CI runners (the bisect output and log formats of git 2.55)
reports.found: 2026-10-26, GitHub Actions run of d2f3b48: ch21/e5_bisect/solution/unittest failed in all six presets (3 of 5 tests) and passed on the reference machine
reports.description: first_bad() parsed the output of 'git bisect run' for 'is the first bad commit' and 'The first bad commit could be any of:'. With git 2.43 on the reference machine it found them; with git 2.55 on the runners it found neither and returned an empty list, so every test that expected a result failed. A first correction (d404166) read 'git bisect log' instead and failed the same way on the runners. A second correction (cdefc06) made first_bad() raise with git's output when it found nothing; that run showed that git 2.55 writes "# first 'bad' commit:" and "# possible first 'bad' commit:" in the log, with the term in quotes, where git 2.43 writes "first bad commit".

evaluation.rationale: An exercise solution, not MiniDAQ code; no release was affected.

resolution.change: The solution and the starter read 'git bisect log' through candidates(), which accepts the term with and without quotes; first_bad() raises with git's output when it finds no candidate; a new test parses a log in each format, so the reference machine checks both. The chapter, the README, the notes and the solutions tell the whole sequence, including the correction that was a guess.
resolution.verification: The solution passes 6 of 6 tests and the starter fails 4 of 6 on the reference machine (git 2.43); the GitHub Actions run of the correcting commit runs the tests with git 2.55.

whys: The bisect tests failed on every runner and passed locally.
first_bad() found no line it looked for in the output or the log of git 2.55.
It parsed text that git formats for people, and git 2.55 changed that text (the messages, and the term quoted in the log).
The test environment had one git version, so nothing showed the dependence.
The first correction was pushed on a guess about the cause, because the tool returned an empty list instead of the evidence.
root_cause.cause: A tool that parsed the text output of another tool as if it were a fixed interface, and hid what it saw when the parse failed.
root_cause.escape: Only one version of git ran the tests before the push; CI was the first to use another, and its failure gave no evidence until the tool reported git's output.

reports.title: Two singles of one crystal with one time stamp were taken in the order they arrived
reports.found: 2026-10-26, release checks for 0.4.0 on commit 78c3d38: Properties.TheOrderOfTiesDoesNotMatter with MINIDAQ_PROP_CASES=100 (case 6752 of seed 3505085556721689392)
reports.description: SRS-SRT-013 asks for the same coincidences, each with the same first and second single, whatever the order of singles with equal times, and the sorter put such singles in crystal order (MDQ-PR-017). Two singles of the same crystal with the same time and different energies stayed in the order they arrived, so the pair's first and second single depended on it. The shrunk counterexample: a fixed 1 ps window, no geometry cut, two singles of crystal 18431 at 0 ps with energies near 435 keV among singles outside the energy window. The 500 cases of the per-commit run had not found it.

evaluation.rationale: The same crystal cannot detect two photons at one time stamp in a real detector (dead time, Chapter 11), so the input does not occur in acquired data; and the swapped pair changes no count, no histogram and no line of response. The defect is a gap between the requirement and the code.

resolution.change: CoincidenceSorter::insert orders singles with equal times by crystal and then by energy, and so does the reference model of the properties; SRS-SRT-013 says so (SRS version 9). A unit test, CoincidenceSorter.TwoSinglesOfOneCrystalWithOneTimeAreTakenInEnergyOrder, keeps the case.
resolution.verification: The unit test fails without the change and passes with it; the replay of the counterexample and the wide search (MINIDAQ_PROP_CASES=100) pass on the release candidate (measurements/release-0.4.0/properties-wide.txt).

whys: Two singles of one crystal with one time came out in the order they arrived.
The sorter's tie rule compared crystals only.
MDQ-PR-017's fix ordered by the key the sort stage uses (time, then crystal), not by a key that is total over the singles.
The per-commit property run (500 cases) rarely draws two singles of one crystal at one time; the wide release search did.
root_cause.cause: A tie-break that was not a total order of the values it had to order.
root_cause.escape: The generator makes equal times common but equal crystals rare, so the per-commit run almost never draws the case; the wider search of the release checks is there for exactly this.

reports.title: The flight recorder's concurrent snapshot test could finish before its writers started
reports.found: 2026-10-26, release checks for 0.4.0 on commit 78c3d38: FlightRecorder.ASnapshotTakenWhileThreadsRecordNeverShowsHalfAnEvent failed in the coverage build (seen == 0)
reports.description: The test starts four writer threads and takes 200 snapshots at once. In the coverage build the snapshots were all taken before any writer had recorded, so the test saw no event and failed its check that it saw some. The test is timing-dependent in the sense of CAPA-0001: its result depended on how fast the threads started.

evaluation.rationale: A defect of a test, not of the recorder; when the test passes it shows what it claims.

resolution.change: The snapshots begin only after every writer has recorded once (a std::latch), so a slow build cannot take them too early; the check that the snapshots saw events stays.
resolution.verification: The test passes in every preset and in the coverage build of the release checks of 0.4.0 (measurements/release-0.4.0/coverage.txt).

whys: The test saw no event.
Its 200 snapshots finished before any writer recorded.
It assumed that threads started with emplace_back run before the next statement of the thread that started them.
Coverage instrumentation slowed the start of the threads enough to break the assumption.
root_cause.cause: A concurrency test whose result depended on the timing of thread start, which CAPA-0001's rule (every wait states why) does not catch, because the test had no wait at all.
root_cause.escape: The other presets start threads fast enough; the coverage build is run only by the release checks.

reports.title: The release checks ended after the writer benchmark with status 0, and the gate, the system tests and the fuzzing never ran
reports.found: 2026-10-26, release checks for 0.4.0 on commit 78c3d38: the output had no line after the writer benchmark and the script's status was 0
reports.description: tools/release_checks.sh ran the writer benchmark in a { } group that ended with 'exit $status'. A group runs in the script's own shell, so the exit ended the whole script, with the benchmark's status: 0 when it ran. Every check after it was skipped: the performance regression gate, the system test report and the soak (added in Chapter 19 and never run in a release), the fuzz build and the seven fuzzing campaigns. The defect came with the gate itself (commit 57ef123, release 0.3.0). The 0.3.0 run stopped at the same place, and its record explained the stop as a restart of the session; the remaining checks were then run by hand, so the 0.3.0 evidence is complete, but the cause was misread and the defect stayed.

evaluation.rationale: No release was made without the checks: 0.3.0 ran the remaining ones by hand, and 0.4.0 is held until a full run passes. The defect is in the verification tool, and it hid itself: a check that never runs reported nothing, which is the failure CAPA-0004 is about.

resolution.change: The writer step runs in a subshell. The script sets a guard on exit: a run that ends before the last check prints a FAIL line and exits with status 3. The test tools.release_checks reads the script for an exit inside a { } group and runs the guard on its own. The 0.3.0 release record has a correction note.
resolution.verification: tools.release_checks fails on the old script and passes on the new one; the release checks of 0.4.0 ran every check to the end (measurements/release-0.4.0/release-checks.txt).

whys: The checks after the writer benchmark did not run.
The writer step's exit ended the script, not the step.
A { } group runs in the current shell, and the step was written as if it were a subshell.
Nothing checked that the script reached its end, and status 0 looked like success.
At 0.3.0 the stop was explained by an event that happened at about the same time (a restart), without evidence that it was the cause.
root_cause.cause: A verification script whose early end looked the same as success, and an anomaly in its first run that was explained instead of investigated.
root_cause.escape: The script had no test of its own (Chapter 20 tests the tools whose output is evidence, but not this one), and its output at 0.3.0 was read for the results of the checks, not for whether all of them were there.

reports.title: Seven controlled documents changed without a new version, and CI skipped the check that finds it
reports.found: 2026-10-26, release checks for 0.4.0 on commit 78c3d38: docs.design_file in ci/run_all.sh, with the local tag book-v0.3.0
reports.description: The editorial change that made the book generic (e50a79e) changed seven controlled documents (intended use, regulatory context, risk management plan, architecture, the change control and CAPA procedures, the threat model) without a new version, which the change control procedure asks for even for editorial changes. The document-control job of CI compares the documents with the last release tag, and the release tags are pushed by hand: GitHub had none, so the job printed 'version check skipped' on every run and passed.

evaluation.rationale: The changes were editorial (names, not content); the defect is in document control, and it was found before the release.

resolution.change: Each document has a new version and a history entry. Without a release tag, the CI job compares with the commit that the newest release record names, so the check cannot be skipped.
resolution.verification: tools/design_file.py --check --since the 0.3.0 commit passes; the document-control job of the correcting commit runs the comparison on GitHub.

whys: The documents changed and kept their versions.
The change was made as a text replacement across the repository, not as a change to each document.
The check that finds it was skipped on GitHub, because it needs a tag that only the reference machine had.
A skipped check printed a line and passed.
root_cause.cause: A check that passes when it cannot run, again (CAPA-0004), and a bulk editorial change that bypassed the per-document step of change control.
root_cause.escape: The local run of docs.design_file uses the local tag and would have failed, but run_all was not run between the editorial change and the release checks.

reports.title: The architecture and the threat model did not describe the diagnostics of Chapter 21
reports.found: 2026-10-26, review of the controlled documents for the release record of 0.4.0
reports.description: CR-0007 (flight recorder, crash report, diagnostics command) named the threat model as affected (a new data flow) but did not change it, and did not list the architecture at all: the architecture still described version 0.3.0-dev, control protocol 2.0 and ADRs 0001 to 0014, and the threat model had no element for the crash report. The threat model's own review rule asks for an update in the review of every change that adds a store or a flow.

evaluation.rationale: The software is unchanged; the analysis of the new store finds no new threat that needs a requirement (T-35 to T-38: environment, not applicable or accepted).

resolution.change: Architecture version 8 (Part IV and the diagnostics, API 2.1, ADR 0016) and threat model version 2 (the crash report store T-35 to T-38, the diagnostics response in T-09, the asset, the data flow diagram).
resolution.verification: docs.threats and docs.design_file pass; the release record of 0.4.0 lists both documents.

whys: The architecture and the threat model lagged the code of Chapter 21.
CR-0007 listed the documents it changed and left out these two.
The change request's Documents section was written from memory of what changed, not checked against the documents that describe the changed elements.
No check ties a new store, flow or command to the threat model or the architecture.
root_cause.cause: A change request whose impact on documents was not checked against the document index.
root_cause.escape: The review of CR-0007 read its list of documents and did not ask which documents describe a server option, a command or a file the change adds.

reports.title: The stress run passed although a test failed in it
reports.found: 2026-10-26, release checks for 0.4.0, part 1 on commit 643cec8: stress-tsan.txt lists a failed test, and the check said pass
reports.description: tools/stress_tests.sh piped ctest's output through grep to keep the lines worth reading, and ended with '|| true' so that a run without such lines would not fail. The script's status was the filter's, never ctest's: a failed test was written to the output file and the stress run passed. The release checks of 0.4.0 reported 'pass  stress run' with AcquisitionService.DefaultAdaptersRunAtTheConfiguredRate failed in it (MDQ-PR-033).

evaluation.rationale: The stress run is release evidence, not a control; the earlier stress outputs (Chapter 16, release 0.3.0) were read and show no failure, so no release relied on a failed run.

resolution.change: The script keeps ctest's status, writes it to the output ('# ctest exit status N') and exits with it. Two tests in tools.release_checks run the script on a build with a failing and with a passing test.
resolution.verification: The old script exits 0 with a failing test, the new one 8; the release checks of 0.4.0 run the corrected script.

whys: The check passed with a failure in its own output.
Its status was the status of the output filter.
A pipeline's status is the status of its last command, and '|| true' was added to keep an empty filter from failing the run.
Nothing tested the script, and its output was read for failures only when the check said FAIL.
root_cause.cause: A verification script whose status did not come from the verification, the third such check found at this release.
root_cause.escape: Chapter 16 wrote the script and read its outputs by eye; the release checks trusted its status.

reports.title: Tests waited 5 or 10 seconds for an acquisition, too short under ThreadSanitizer and load
reports.found: 2026-10-26, release checks for 0.4.0, the stress run (ThreadSanitizer, 8 busy loops on 4 CPUs): AcquisitionService.DefaultAdaptersRunAtTheConfiguredRate
reports.description: The test paces 200,000 singles at 2 M/s and waits up to 5 s for the run to end. Under the stress run the run took longer and the wait failed. Eighteen waits in five test files had fixed deadlines of 5 or 10 s, and test_support::patience, the deadline that only a hang should reach, was 10 s. Rule 5.5 asks for a deadline long enough that only a hang reaches it; 5 s is not that under ThreadSanitizer on a loaded machine.

evaluation.rationale: A defect of tests: the code under test was slow because of the sanitizer and the load, not wrong.

resolution.change: Every wait uses test_support::patience, now 60 s. A passing test does not wait longer; only a hang does.
resolution.verification: The stress run of the release checks of 0.4.0 passes 100 repetitions of the threaded tests.

whys: The wait ended before the run did.
Its deadline was 5 s, chosen as 'long' on an idle machine.
The tests chose their own deadlines instead of the shared one.
The shared one, 10 s, was itself chosen without measuring the slowest build under load.
root_cause.cause: Deadlines picked by feel instead of from the slowest configuration that runs them.
root_cause.escape: Rule 5.5's check (tests.waits) finds sleeps, not short deadlines; the stress run found it, and MDQ-PR-032 hid it.

reports.title: Exercise 5.2's speed test asked for exactly its goal, three times the starter's speed, and failed on a runner at 2.99
reports.found: 2026-10-26, GitHub Actions run of 3849498: ch05/e2_hotspot/solution/EventSource.FastEnough failed in the preset hardened at 14.49 ns per single against a budget of 14.43 ns (reference 43.3 ns); the other presets and the next commit passed
reports.description: MDQ-PR-022 made the budget relative: a third of the time of the starter's algorithm, timed in the same run. That is the exercise's goal, and the solution reaches it with a ratio of 3.7 or more on the reference machine, but in the hardened build on a GitHub runner the ratio was 2.99. A test that asks for exactly what the solution achieves on some machine fails there by chance.

evaluation.rationale: An exercise test, not a test of MiniDAQ; it failed a correct solution and could not pass a slow one.

resolution.change: The test asks for half the time of the starter's algorithm; the exercise's goal stays a third. Its README, Chapter 5, the solution notes and Chapter 20 say why.
resolution.verification: The solution passes in all six presets of the release checks and in CI; the starter still fails (its ratio is about 1).

whys: The solution measured 2.99 times the starter's speed against a criterion of 3.
The criterion was the exercise's goal itself, with no margin.
MDQ-PR-022 fixed the kind of criterion (relative instead of absolute) and kept its value.
No rule asked for a margin between what a speed test demands and what a correct solution reaches on the slowest machine that runs it.
root_cause.cause: A speed criterion without a margin for the machines that run it.
root_cause.escape: The reference machine leaves a margin of about 20%; the hardened build on a runner had none, and only one of six presets failed once.
